element: The nucleotide immediately 3' of the stop codon -- the fourth position of the stop tetranucleotide. Readthrough-permissive contexts (canonically a pyrimidine, notably C, after TGA) reduce NMD; among selected ORFs TGA is 50.9% of stops, TAA 26.8%, TAG 22.3%, so all strata are well populated.
test: Stage 1: train a structure-only model (fusion takes struct_emb alone, Linear(32 -> 64)) to convergence; this is the tabular predictor whose GBM analogue already reaches AUPRC 0.8035. Stage 2: rebuild the full 96-wide fusion, copy stage 1's weights into the struct columns 64:96, freeze struct_fc and those columns, precompute each isoform's stage-1 logit and add it DETACHED as a fixed offset inside BCEWithLogitsLoss, and train the conv branches and their fusion columns. State plainly that this removes the incentive to re-encode structure, not the possibility. Operator on the trained models: single-base substitution at +4 of slot 0's stop, GC-matched only (C<->G and A<->T, the two operator classes shown here to have a reference approaching null), per isoform, stratified by stop triplet, gated on slot 0 being EJC-triggering (n_downstream_ejc >= 1 with nearest downstream junction > 50 nt -- 7,492 slot-0 ORFs qualify).
matched_reference: (1) Noise floor: the same GC-matched operator at +7, +10 and +13 -- same codon phase, same substitution type, mechanistically inert -- plus the 37 banked frame-matched control positions. (2) Other positions: the +4 effect must exceed those positions in the same isoform, not merely differ from zero. (3) Matched population: the same operator at +4 in the NON-EJC-triggering stratum (the 15,765 PTC- no-trigger isoforms), where readthrough has nothing to rescue; an equal-sized effect there means we measured a base preference, which is precisely how the Kozak +4 claim failed.
would_refute: If the residual-regime +4 effect is no larger than the jointly trained model's, and neither separates from the +7/+10/+13 controls after per-isoform gating, the element is not usable in this model and the 'less central contributors' of section 2 should be dropped from the paper rather than reported weakly. If the effect appears equally in the non-triggering stratum, it is a base preference and refutes the readthrough mechanism.

title: Minimal in-frame stop implant: does the model carry the 50-nt rule, or only a receptive-field-truncated version of it?
element: An in-frame stop triplet (TAA/TAG/TGA) created by a 3-nt substitution at distance d upstream of a specific exon-exon junction. The element is a PTC defined by its JUNCTION OFFSET d, not by junction count — the canonical NMD positional element, and the one thing the model's tabular block provably does not contain.
test: Backgrounds: the 15,765 PTC-negative no-trigger isoforms (2.2% NMD+), filtered to ORF length <= 2000 nt so the w2000 ATG+stop windows partition the whole ORF and the transcript sequence is exactly reconstructable from H5 channels 0-3 (no FASTA needed — verified locally missing). Choose isoforms with an internal CDS inter-junction interval of >=150 nt. TREATMENT: at each in-frame codon position across that interval, substitute the codon with a stop. CONTROL: substitute the same three positions with each of the <=7 W/S-class-preserving recodings of that stop (TGA -> {TGT,TCA,TCT,AGA,AGT,ACA,ACT}; TAA -> the 7 other A/T triples). These hold G/C-vs-A/T identity at every position, so compute_rolling_gc's is_gc vector is unchanged and channel 5 is BITWISE identical; channels 4 and 6-8 are untouched. Then RE-SCAN, which is the part no existing script does: recompute the truncated ORF's new stop, recompute n_downstream_ejc from junctions.tsv, recompute frac_stop, move the ORF-midpoint clip (mid = (atg+stop)//2 shifts because the ORF shortened) and re-encode both windows via encode_window_v5. Score with all 5 atg2000_stop2000 seed checkpoints in results_4ct_sweep. Run a second, explicitly off-manifold PINNED arm with n_downstream_ejc held at its pre-edit value, purely to split the total effect into a tabular path and a window path. THE CONFOUNDER I have to break: within one isoform, d and the ORF-truncation length move together, and the midpoint clip moves with them. Break it by panel design — across ~300 backgrounds with junctions at different CDS positions, d and truncation length are not collinear, so a per-isoform-then-pooled regression of delta on (d, truncation length, frac_stop) separates them.
matched_reference: Three references, one per failure mode named in trap 1. (1) METHOD NOISE FLOOR: the W/S-class-preserving recodings at the identical three positions — identical frame offset, identical junction channel, and channel 5 exactly, not approximately, preserved. This is adjacent to the dead 'dinucleotide-preserving shuffle of a 3-mer' and escapes it precisely: that shuffle is the identity map because 100% of 3-mers have one arrangement, whereas a per-position class-preserving RECODE has 2^3 = 8 members, 7 of them non-identity, and unlike a shuffle it guarantees position-wise GC identity. (2) OTHER POSITIONS: the d sweep itself — every stop implant in the interval is a control for every other, and they share composition, frame and n_downstream_ejc, so only d differs. (3) MATCHED POPULATION: backgrounds matched on tx_length, ORF length, interval width and GC; the d effect must survive the joint regression against truncation length.
would_refute: A flat delta(d) inside intervals, with all the response appearing only when d crosses a junction (i.e. only when n_downstream_ejc increments), refutes it: the model would then represent the trigger solely as an EJC count and carry no positional element at all. Equally refuting: the stop implant's effect equals the W/S recodes' effect, meaning the response is to having edited three bases rather than to having created a stop. Or the pinned arm zeroing the effect, which would show the window path contributes nothing and the sequence-element claim collapses to a tabular feature. The false-negative risk (trap 7) is a badly chosen panel: if intervals are short the d range never reaches the transition, so interval width >=150 nt is a precondition, not a nicety.

title: The 1-nt frame triplet: an implanted uAUG's frame is the treatment and its composition is the control
element: An ATG triplet implanted in the 5'UTR at offset o. The element is the AUG together with its FRAME relative to the reference AUG: frame 0 creates an N-terminal extension (mechanistically inert), frames 1 and 2 create a competing ORF that is either a 5'UTR-terminating uORF (leaky, reinitiation-rescued) or an oORF reading past the main AUG out of frame and terminating inside the CDS (no rescue, the potent class).
test: Backgrounds: PTC-negative no-trigger isoforms with >=200 nt of 5'UTR reconstructable from the w2000 ATG window. At each candidate 5'UTR offset, implant ATG at o, o+1 and o+2 — three arms, same three bases, same distance from the cap, same background. Length-preserving substitution, so junction positions, tx_length and every native ORF's coordinates are untouched. Re-scan to derive the created ORF: walk in frame to the first in-frame stop, require >= 33 nt (the ORFik floor, min_orf_length 9 codons confirmed in orf_scan_metadata.json), and classify uORF / oORF / extension from where that stop falls. Run in TWO modes. ADDITIVE: append the created ORF as a 6th slot — the checkpoint is permutation-invariant across slots and has no K-dependent parameter, so a (batch, 6, 9, W) tensor runs unchanged — which isolates the added ORF without confounding it with the eviction of a native ORF. COMPETITIVE: let it contest a slot under the native ref-CDS / TD2 / top-Kozak priority rule, which is the realistic ribosome-competition setting. Report both; the difference between them is the selection component. GC matching (trap 2): the three arms replace different triplets, so their net GC change differs — restrict to offsets where the three replaced triplets have equal GC content, which is an implementable filter, and report the retained fraction. Frame-offset matching of controls (trap 3) is automatic here because frame is the treatment and everything else is held. Also match on created-ORF length across arms, or carry it as a covariate, since frame determines where the first in-frame stop falls.
matched_reference: The frame triplet IS the matched reference and it is unusually tight: the three arms are the same three nucleotides at offsets differing by one, so composition, distance from cap, background identity, native ORF set and slot count are all identical, and one arm (in-frame) is a mechanistic null by biology rather than by construction. That single-slot addition is common to all three arms, so the attention-dilution artifact that killed inference-time flag ablation cancels exactly in the paired contrast — the dilution enters all three arms identically and subtracts out. Second reference: an added slot carrying a native non-triggering ORF, to check that any added slot with a high EJC count does not produce the same shift regardless of frame. Third: matched population on 5'UTR length, native kozak_score at the implant site, and GC.
would_refute: delta(oORF) ~ delta(uORF) ~ delta(extension) refutes it — the model would be responding to slot addition, not to a competing ORF. So would an ordering that tracks only the created ORF's n_downstream_ejc irrespective of frame, or a result that vanishes in the competitive mode (meaning the finding is an artifact of running at K=6). This is adjacent to the dead 'frame-rotation probes: off-manifold, and rotate-by-3 is the identity' and escapes it because no channel is rotated: the ATG is physically moved by one nucleotide, every arm is a real transcript sequence, and channels 6-8 are recomputed from the re-derived ORF start rather than permuted. Per trap 8, the claim is capped at 'changes the model's ORF selection and verdict', not 'changes ribosome selection', absent ribosome profiling.

title: GC-frozen in-silico evolution of a maximally NMD-inducing 30-mer, with the in-frame stop codon as its own built-in positive control
element: The evolved 30-nt string itself, implanted at a fixed frame-matched offset. The discovery output is a named, localizable sequence: whatever wins is reported as a string with its frame phase and its offset to the reference AUG and to the nearest junction, then matched against known elements (in-frame stop, uAUG, splice-donor-like, poly-U/AU-rich, GC run).
test: (1+lambda) evolution strategy or simulated annealing over a 30-nt string. Fitness = the median per-isoform delta log-odds across a panel of B ~ 200 naive backgrounds (PTC-negative, no-trigger), median rather than mean so one runaway background cannot drive the search. MUTATION OPERATOR: only W/S-class-preserving swaps (A<->T, G<->C at a position). This freezes GC content by construction and, because compute_rolling_gc derives is_gc per base, freezes channel 5 BITWISE for the entire search — the optimizer physically cannot cheat by becoming GC-rich, which is the failure trap 2 says has already produced confident structure at every position under a G-vs-not-G operator. Seed multiple independent random starts at several fixed GC levels so GC is a stratum, not a free parameter. Implant offset held fixed and frame-matched across the whole search, and edits forbidden within 50 nt of any window boundary or of the ORF-midpoint clip so the search cannot win by exploiting padding transitions. TWO ARMS: RE-SCANNED (the created ORF structure is re-derived and the tabular block recomputed — biologically faithful, and the arm where the stop-codon positive control can fire) and FROZEN-ANNOTATION (window edit only, tabular block pinned). The difference between the two arms localizes how much of the discoverable signal is a sequence readout versus a route into the pre-computed structural summary — which is exactly the 'pre-computed away' problem named in brief section 2. HELD-OUT VALIDATION: evolve using members 1-4 only, then evaluate the winner on member 5, which never entered the fitness function, and on a disjoint background panel drawn from held-out chromosomes.
matched_reference: (1) NOISE FLOOR: the same search, same operator, same generation budget, optimizing a FIXED RANDOM LINEAR FUNCTIONAL of the 64-dim transcript embedding instead of the NMD logit. This yields the fitness gain and convergence sharpness attributable to search pressure alone on this architecture, which no permuted-label null can supply (permuted-label FDR at the causal gate is dead because the null count is ~0 by construction). (2) OTHER POSITIONS: the same evolved winner implanted at frame-shifted and junction-distal offsets. (3) MATCHED POPULATION: held-out-chromosome backgrounds matched on tx_length, ORF length and GC. Cross-member concordance is used only as an OUT-OF-SAMPLE TRANSFER test to a member excluded from optimization, never as sign agreement at a position — the latter is dead because members agree 65-92% at meaningless control positions against a 6.25% chance rate, whereas a winner optimized on four members failing on the fifth is the ordinary fate of adversarial sequences and so is genuinely informative.
would_refute: The winner failing to transfer to the held-out member or the held-out backgrounds refutes it — that is an adversarial artifact, not an element. So does the re-scanned search failing to rediscover the in-frame stop codon: the positive control not firing means the instrument cannot find the element we know is there, and no other output from it should be believed. So does the search converging no faster and no higher than the random-functional control, or converging on something that sits at a window boundary despite the exclusion zone.

title: uAUG copy-number dose response, routed through the slot channel because global max pooling makes the CNN copy-blind
element: A cluster of k AUG triplets (k = 0..4) at spaced 5'UTR offsets, each initiating a PTC-bearing upstream ORF. The element is the MULTIPLICITY, not any single AUG — the ATF4/ATF5/GCN4 architecture in which the number of uORFs, not their existence, sets the regulatory output.
test: Backgrounds: PTC-negative no-trigger isoforms with >= 400 nt of 5'UTR. Implant k ATGs at spaced offsets (>= 60 nt apart so their created ORFs are distinct), length-preserving, then re-scan each created ORF and keep only backgrounds where all k are valid (>= 33 nt) and PTC-bearing. Run at K = 5 + k so no native ORF is evicted — the checkpoint has no K-dependent parameter and is permutation-invariant across slots, so K = 6..9 runs unchanged. MATCHED CONTROL ARM: k IN-FRAME ATGs at the same offsets, which create k N-terminal extensions — identical composition, identical number of implanted bases, identical slot count, identical softmax dilution, no PTC. Sweep k = 0,1,2,3,4 within each background. SEPARATE POSITIVE CONTROL FOR THE ARCHITECTURE CLAIM: implant k copies of a single motif inside ONE window with no new slot created, and confirm the response is flat — that measures the max-pool blindness empirically instead of assuming it, and validates that any dose response seen in the main design is the slot channel.
matched_reference: The k in-frame extension arm, which is the whole design. It matches composition base-for-base, matches slot count exactly, and therefore cancels the attention-dilution artifact that killed inference-time flag ablation as a measure of sequence contribution — that method failed because dilution shrank control positions (0.66x) alongside targets (0.42x), and here dilution is identical in treatment and control at every k and subtracts out of the paired difference. Second reference: the single-window copy sweep, which supplies the architecture's own null. Third: matched population on 5'UTR length, GC and native uAUG count (n_upstream_atgs is already in selected_orfs.tsv), since backgrounds that already have uAUGs are not naive with respect to this element.
would_refute: A flat or non-monotone paired curve refutes the graded hypothesis: the model would treat uORFs as a binary presence indicator. A curve that saturates at k = 1 says the same. A treatment curve that is not separable from the extension curve says the response is to slot addition, not to competing ORFs. The specific false-negative risk to declare (trap 7): a negative here may be a property of the training data rather than of the model, because the 33-nt floor excluded the short regulatory uORFs and only 5 of a mean 36.6 ORFs per isoform are kept — so a negative must be reported as 'this model, trained on this ORF universe, has no graded uORF response', and it names the fix (lower the floor, raise K, retrain).

title: Minimal-flip search under a GC-isomorphic operator: how few bases flip a confident prediction, and do they land where the mechanism says
element: The minimal set of W/S-class-preserving substitutions that flips a confidently predicted isoform, reported not as positions but as the triplets it creates and destroys — in-frame stops, upstream AUGs, stop-codon readthrough — together with each edit's offset to the reference AUG, to the stop, and to the nearest junction.
test: Take ~300 high-confidence non-NMD test-set isoforms and ~300 high-confidence NMD isoforms (the extremes of predictions_atg500_stop500.tsv, re-scored with the sweep ensemble), restricted to ORF length <= 2000 nt so sequence is reconstructable from w2000 channels 0-3. Greedy or beam search (beam ~8) over substitution SETS: at each step evaluate every single W/S-class-preserving substitution over the reconstructable extent, take the best, repeat until the ensemble prediction crosses 0.5 or a budget of 20 edits is exhausted. The operator matters as much as the search: because compute_rolling_gc derives is_gc per base, a W/S-preserving substitution leaves channel 5 bitwise unchanged, so the search cannot buy a flip with composition and any flip it finds is an identity-of-base effect. RE-SCANNED mode throughout — after each accepted edit, re-derive the ORF's stop, recompute n_downstream_ejc from junctions.tsv, recompute frac_start/frac_stop, move the midpoint clip and re-encode. Cost per isoform is bounded by (budget x positions x 1 alternative per position, since W/S-preserving means each position has exactly one alternative) — roughly 20 x 2000 = 40k scored transcripts per isoform per member, which is ~10x a full single-base ISM (measured at 8.77 s/isoform/member for both branches at W=1000), so ~90 s per isoform per member; 600 isoforms x 5 members is ~75 CPU-hours, parallelizable to a few hours.
matched_reference: (1) METHOD NOISE FLOOR: the identical search, identical operator, identical budget, optimizing a FIXED RANDOM LINEAR FUNCTIONAL of the 64-dim transcript embedding. This gives the edit-count distribution and edit-location histogram produced by search pressure alone against this architecture and this operator, which is exactly the null that permuted labels cannot provide (dead: the null count is ~0 by construction at the causal gate). Because the null search has the same search-induced structure, an excess of mechanism-consistent first edits over it is interpretable. (2) OTHER POSITIONS: within each isoform, the runner-up edits at each greedy step — their location distribution is the within-isoform reference for the accepted edit. (3) MATCHED POPULATION: flip-up and flip-down cohorts matched on ORF length, tx_length, GC and n_downstream_ejc, so 'fewer edits needed' cannot be a proxy for a shorter or more junction-dense transcript.
would_refute: Edit locations statistically indistinguishable from the random-functional control refutes it. So does a first-edit category distribution with no enrichment for stop creation or uAUG creation. So does a flip-down search that never touches the annotated stop. And a sharply asymmetric result — flip-down cheap and mechanistic, flip-up expensive and scattered — would refute the symmetric form of the hypothesis while still being informative, since it would say the model represents trigger destruction but not trigger creation. Two confounders to exclude before believing any positive, per trap 7: edits clustering at window boundaries or at the ORF-midpoint clip (forbid a 50-nt exclusion zone at every boundary and report how many candidate edits that removes), and edits that flip the prediction only through the recomputed tabular block (run the pinned-tabular decomposition on the final edit set and report the split).

title: Optimus-5-Prime transfer: the joint start-codon context surface, scored against an external MPRA initiation scale, flips sign with the slot's PTC status
element: The 6-nt start-codon context at positions −6..−1 of a candidate AUG (the gccRcc half of gccRccAUGG), treated as a single 4^6 element rather than as independent bases. Claim: a high-initiation-efficiency context on an AUG whose own stop is EJC-triggering INCREASES NMD susceptibility; the same context on an AUG whose stop is not EJC-triggering decreases it.
test: Optimus-5-Prime enumeration in real backgrounds, not a fixed random one. For N=500 isoforms (test split, gene-clustered sample, stratified so ~half have an EJC-triggering slot-0 stop), enumerate all 4^6=4096 assignments of positions −6..−1 in the ATG window of slot 0, recompute channel 5 over the filled extent by the existing exact path (measure_position_bank.recompute_gc), score under all five checkpoints. orf_start, frame channels 6–8, junction channel 4 and the whole 5-number tabular block are provably invariant under this perturbation, so nothing needs re-deriving. Exclusion, applied identically to target and decoy and recorded per frame offset (trap 3): drop any context creating an ATG at any of the four in-window offsets, ~6% of 4096. Repeat the identical enumeration at a DECOY: a frame-matched, non-AUG position ≥90 nt further 5' in the same window, same exclusion mask, same recomputation. Optional 4^8 extension adding +4..+5 if the 4^6 result is positive.
matched_reference: Three, as trap 1 demands. (1) Noise floor: the identical 4096-context enumeration at a frame-matched decoy position in the same window and same isoform, carrying identical composition variation, identical GC recomputation and the identical ATG-creation exclusion mask, so any correlation arising from the model's global GC/base preferences appears there too. (2) Other positions: the rho_i profile as the decoy is walked from −12 to −120 nt; a real Kozak signal must be localised to the true context. (3) Matched population: the EJC-triggering vs non-triggering strata are the same isoforms perturbed by the identical operator, so a sign difference between strata cannot be produced by composition. Additionally the external scale is a direct MPRA measurement of initiation, which is what lets this escape trap 8: the readout is not 'predicts the annotated start' (circular, capped) but 'tracks measured initiation efficiency', a quantity no annotation in this pipeline encodes. Composition is further excluded by partial Spearman on context GC and by re-running within the fixed-GC stratum (contexts with exactly 3 of 6 G+C).
would_refute: median rho_i indistinguishable from the decoy distribution in both strata; or rho_i significant but equal in the triggering and non-triggering strata (a start-context preference with no NMD content); or rho_i collapsing to zero under partial correlation on context GC and inside the fixed-GC stratum, meaning the surface is composition, not Kozak. A negative is interpretable only if the positive control fires: the same pipeline applied to the tabular is_ref_cds bit must move predictions strongly.

title: Saluki-style insertional analysis at the stop: the termination tetranucleotide, probed with a mononucleotide-permutation operator (UAG<->UGA) that no single-base contrast can express
element: The stop tetranucleotide — the stop trinucleotide plus the +4 base (UAAN/UAGN/UGAN). Claim: a TIGHT termination context (UAA, and +4 G) at an EJC-triggering stop increases NMD susceptibility; the leaky context UGA-C decreases it.
test: For each isoform in the population (N~2,000: slot-0 ORFs, ~half PTC+ from build_mechanism_classes.py's reference-AUG-anchored classes, ~half PTC- no-trigger), substitute the stop window's centre trinucleotide with each of TAA/TAG/TGA and the +4 base with each of A/C/G/T — 12 contexts, x5 members, x2 arms (target, and a frame-matched decoy: the same 12 four-mers written over an in-frame sense codon 30 nt upstream in the same window, where they are not termination signals). Recompute channel 5 by the exact path. THE PERTURBATION IS ORF-INVARIANT BY CONSTRUCTION: substituting one stop for another leaves orf_start, orf_end, frame channels, the junction channel and all five tabular numbers — including n_downstream_ejc — bitwise unchanged, so this is the only sequence element in the model that can be probed with zero recomputation of anything structural. Headline operator is the composition permutation TAG<->TGA: same multiset {T,A,G}, identical G+C count, so every 50-nt rolling window fully containing the codon has an identical GC value and only ~2 of ~500 positions differ, by 0.02. Secondary: +4 G vs C (the project's own GC-matched secondary operator, reported against its known G-preference baseline).
matched_reference: (1) Noise floor: the same 12-context substitution at the frame-matched in-window decoy codon, which carries identical composition change and identical recomputation but is not a termination signal. (2) Other positions: the decoy walked to three offsets (-30, -60, -90 nt), so the effect must be localised to the actual stop. (3) Matched population: PTC+ vs PTC- no-trigger isoforms perturbed with the IDENTICAL operator; composition cannot generate a stratum difference because the operator, exclusion mask and recomputation are byte-identical across strata. This is the same logic that made the brief's 'Kozak sign follows the slot's PTC status' result credible, applied to an element where the operator is composition-exact. Explicit escape from section 6: TAG<->TGA is a MONOnucleotide-preserving permutation, not the dinucleotide-preserving 3-mer shuffle that is the identity map — TAG has dinucleotides {TA,AG}, TGA has {TG,GA}, so they are distinct sequences with identical base composition. The dead method fails because it produces no perturbation; this one produces a perturbation with composition held exactly.
would_refute: Paired Δ(TGA)-Δ(TAG) with a median indistinguishable from the decoy arm; or an effect the same size in PTC+ and PTC- isoforms (a stop-codon preference with no NMD content — very plausible, since TGA usage correlates with gene GC and the model may have absorbed that as a marginal); or a per-isoform Spearman against the readthrough scale no better than against a shuffled scale. Positive control that must fire before any negative is reported: substituting the stop trinucleotide for a SENSE codon must move predictions by orders of magnitude more (reported as a sanity signal only, since ORF-invariance no longer covers it).

title: BPNet-style syntax scan: a purine-rich exonic element at -24..-20 of a downstream junction raises that junction's NMD potency
element: A GA-rich SRSF1-type octamer (GAAGAAGA and measured ESE relatives) implanted in the exonic sequence 5' of a downstream exon-exon junction, with an effect that PEAKS at offset ~-22 nt and is flat elsewhere. The element is a junction-potentiating enhancer, so it increases NMD susceptibility only when a junction is present.
test: Select N~800 isoforms whose slot-0 stop window's downstream half contains exactly ONE junction mark, at >=50 nt from the stop (NMD-competent by the rule) and >=60 nt from the window edge. Implant the octamer by replacing 8 native bases at each offset o in {-40,...,+40} relative to the junction, one offset at a time; recompute channel 5 exactly; score under all five members. Two arms, identical in every other respect: ARM A leaves the junction mark in place; ARM B zeroes channel 4 at that single position while holding n_downstream_ejc at its observed value. The readout is the DIFFERENCE of the two offset profiles. Implant variants at each offset: (i) the octamer, (ii) a dinucleotide-preserving shuffle of the same octamer — an 8-mer has many valid arrangements, so this is a real control and not the identity map that killed the 3-mer version, (iii) a G+C-count-matched random octamer redrawn per isoform. Exclusions applied identically across variants and recorded per frame offset (trap 3): drop implants creating an in-frame stop or any ATG.
matched_reference: (1) Noise floor: the dinucleotide-preserving shuffle and the GC-count-matched random octamer at the same offset in the same isoform — identical replacement footprint, identical composition, only identity differs. (2) Other positions: the profile's own out-of-band region |o|>25, which the 42-nt receptive field says MUST be flat; a peak outside +/-21 is a positive artifact detector that fails the experiment rather than confirming it. (3) Matched population: ARM B, the same isoform with the junction mark erased, sweeping identical distances-from-stop with identical implants — the reference that excludes the dominant alternative, that the profile merely tracks distance to the stop. Explicit escape from section 6: the brief kills 'inference-time flag ablation as a measure of sequence contribution' because it shrinks controls (0.66x) alongside targets (0.42x), i.e. it measures attention dilution. Here the erased-junction run is not the measurement; it is the control ARM of an implant scan, and the reported quantity is a DIFFERENCE OF TWO IMPLANT PROFILES within the arm pair. Any uniform attention-dilution factor multiplies both arms' profiles and cancels in the argmax, and is estimated directly from the out-of-band baseline for the height statistic.
would_refute: A flat ARM A minus ARM B difference profile; or a peak that survives in the dinucleotide-shuffle control (a replacement-footprint effect, not a motif); or a peak whose argmax distribution is uniform over +/-21 (an interaction with no positional structure — the model knows 'junction nearby' but not where); or a peak outside +/-21, which the receptive field forbids and which would indict the harness. Reported negative only if a positive control fires: implanting a junction MARK in channel 4 at o instead of a sequence motif must produce a large, offset-dependent effect.

title: SpliceAI receptive-field transfer: is the ~50-nt rule representable in the sequence branch at all? Column-drop retrain plus a dilated stop branch, then a junction-relocation scan
element: The positional element itself: the >=50-nt junction-free spacer between the stop codon and the next exon-exon junction. Claim: this spacing — not any motif — is the largest sequence-encoded determinant of NMD susceptibility, and its empirical boundary in lung-cell NMD data is a measurable number the current model cannot hold.
test: Three stages. STAGE 1, current checkpoints, no training: for isoforms with a single junction in the stop window's downstream half, relocate that junction MARK in channel 4 across d in {5,10,...,200} nt from the stop, sequence untouched, in two conditions — (a) n_downstream_ejc held at its observed value, isolating what the sequence branch alone does with position, and (b) n_downstream_ejc recomputed consistently with the moved mark, the positive control, which must produce a large step. Plot per-isoform Δlog-odds vs d. STAGE 2, retrain: DROP n_downstream_ejc from the tabular block — n_orf_features 5->4, which model.py already supports natively as its default — and retrain five members. This is a column drop, not zeroing: section 6 kills naive zeroing because with the input identically zero dL/dW = delta * x^T = 0 exactly and the branch becomes a learned constant; removing the input dimension removes the weight, so there is nothing to freeze. The information is not removed — channel 4 still carries every junction — only the pre-computed summary is. STAGE 3: retrain five more members with the stop branch's conv2 dilated (dilation 2, k2=7, receptive field ~66 nt > 50) and re-run the Stage-1 scan on both retrained ensembles.
matched_reference: (1) Noise floor: relocating the mark to positions UPSTREAM of the stop within the same window, where the rule does not apply by mechanism, must give a flat curve. (2) Other positions: the d-sweep is its own positional reference — the null is 'no d-dependence' and the alternative is 'a step', so the shape carries the claim. (3) Matched population: the same scan on isoforms whose stop is the reference CDS stop and on isoforms where it is a PTC; the boundary must appear in both if it is a property of the spacing rather than of the isoform class. Across the three ensembles (published, column-dropped, column-dropped + dilated) the population, split, labels and windows are byte-identical, so the only differences are the tabular column and the receptive field.
would_refute: Stage 1 showing a sharp step at ~50 nt in condition (a) with n_downstream_ejc frozen would falsify the receptive-field argument and would need explaining — most likely a leak via frame channels, transcript-end padding, or a junction-density proxy in channel 5, each checkable. Stage 3 showing no d-dependence even after the column is dropped and the receptive field widened would say the model cannot learn the rule from junction marks at all, and that structural dominance is representational rather than merely convenient. Stage 2 showing NO AUPRC drop would mean n_downstream_ejc was redundant all along, contradicting the measured 59-78% structural share. Against trap 7: a Stage-1 negative is PREDICTED by the architecture and so is weak evidence alone — reportable only alongside condition (b) firing, which proves the harness can move the model.

title: Saluki/BPNet pipeline with the dead component swapped: composition-centred ISM tracks -> TF-MoDISco seqlets -> implant validation in naive backgrounds
element: De novo seqlets, unnamed in advance, with three pre-registered predictions so the result can be wrong: (i) in the stop window, the termination tetranucleotide and an AT-rich hexamer near the transcript 3' end (AAUAAA); (ii) in the ATG window, a GA-rich element 5' of the AUG; (iii) in the stop window's downstream half, a purine-rich element within +/-25 nt of a junction mark. Any seqlet reaching stage 3 is a named, localised, causally validated sequence element.
test: Three stages, mirroring Saluki's ISM + insertional analysis and BPNet's attribution + MoDISco + implant, with DeepSHAP replaced by ISM. STAGE 1: full single-base ISM on N=500 isoforms (gene-clustered, stratified over the four mechanism classes), both branches, all five members, using the existing exact machinery — the measured no-op floor is 3.3e-5 and recomputed-GC agreement with stored channel 5 is 2.4e-4, i.e. float16 storage precision. ISM has exact completeness by construction, which is the whole reason it replaces DeepSHAP (completeness error 129-307% of the effect it decomposed). STAGE 2: build MoDISco input as COMPOSITION-CENTRED hypothetical contributions — at each position subtract the mean of the 4 base-substitution Δ values, removing the 'all four bases move together' term that IS the rolling-GC/composition confound of trap 2, leaving only base-identity preference. This is the same operator logic that made A_vs_T the project's only near-null contrast (control |mean| 0.00111, |t| 1.00), generalised to all four bases. Gate PER ISOFORM before pooling (trap 4): an isoform's positions enter the seqlet pool only where |centred Δ| exceeds the 95th percentile of that same isoform's own control-position distribution. Run TF-MoDISco on the gated tracks, separately for the ATG and stop branches and separately by mechanism class. STAGE 3, which makes it evidence rather than a picture: every seqlet with >=50 supporting instances is implanted with the proposal-3 harness into 300 NAIVE backgrounds — isoforms that contributed no seqlet instance — at a sweep of anchor-relative offsets, against its dinucleotide-preserving shuffle and a GC-count-matched random k-mer of the same length.
matched_reference: (1) Noise floor: the measured no-op floor (3.3e-5) and the method floor at production batch size (~7e-7), plus each isoform's own control-position distribution, which is what the gate thresholds against. (2) Other positions: MoDISco run identically on ISM tracks of the SAME windows restricted to positions >150 nt from either anchor, where the biology predicts no anchor-related element; seqlets recovered there are the artifact class and calibrate how many seqlets this pipeline manufactures from nothing. (3) Matched population: Stage 3's naive backgrounds — isoforms contributing no instance of the seqlet — the only reference that can distinguish 'the model reacts to this because it co-occurs with something' from 'this element causes the shift'. Explicit non-use of permuted-label FDR: section 6 kills it at the causal gate because the null count is ~0 by construction; the nulls here are the distant-position MoDISco run and the per-seqlet shuffle control, both with non-degenerate null distributions.
would_refute: MoDISco's top seqlets being GC-extremal k-mers with no positional concentration — the composition confound surviving the centring, and the outcome TF-MoDISco is most criticised for. Or seqlets recovered at the same rate from the >150-nt distant-position control run. Or seqlets that consolidate cleanly but produce no effect above their own dinucleotide-shuffle when implanted into naive backgrounds, meaning the ISM peaks were background-specific epistasis and not elements. None of the three pre-registered predictions being recovered is itself a clean negative and is the most likely single outcome.

title: The out-of-frame upstream AUG: an identical-3-mer implant whose only variable is codon phase, refereed by gnomAD depletion of uAUG-creating SNVs
element: The trinucleotide ATG located in the 5'UTR at a codon phase != 0 relative to the slot's own start codon (an oORF/uORF-creating uAUG), as against the identical ATG at phase 0 (an N-terminal extension). Named, localizable to a single transcript index, and mechanistically the distinction the brief draws in section 2.
test: (1) Implant bank. N=1,500 isoforms with ref_atg_available and ref_utr5_length >= 150 (23,306 qualify; 13,049 have >= 300 nt), slot 0, ATG window at W=2000 so the upstream reach is 1000 nt and is clipped only by the transcript start (the midpoint clip binds only inward -- data_prep.py encode_transcript_orfs, limit_hi=mid). At every filled index p in [-300,-10] relative to the start codon's A, write ATG over p, p+1, p+2 and recompute channel 5 with the exact recompute_gc used in analysis_plans/measure_position_bank.py. Channels 4 and 6-8 are geometric and are NOT touched. (2) The operator. The implanted 3-mer is IDENTICAL at all three phases -- only its position moves by 1 nt. Composition is therefore exactly matched, and the rolling-GC channel differs only through a <=2 nt shift of the single G, i.e. at <=4 of 2000 indices by 1/51 each, against 51 indices x 1/51 for any single-base G-vs-A operator. Run a second GC-frozen arm (channel 5 held at pre-implant values); if the phase contrast survives both arms, composition is excluded. (3) Frame-matched exclusions (trap 3). Drop (isoform,p) where the implant creates or destroys an in-frame stop, destroys a pre-existing ATG, or falls within 3 nt of a junction mark; report exclusion rate PER PHASE and drop any p whose per-phase rates differ, rather than reweighting. (4) Stratify phase-0 implants on whether an in-frame stop lies between the implant and the main AUG -- a phase-0 ATG with an intervening stop is a real 5'UTR uORF, not an extension, and must not be pooled into the null arm. (5) External arm. Lift transcript index to genome via gencode.v49.primary_assembly.annotation.sorted.gtf.gz (ENST, 16,068 isoforms) or nmd_isocall_4ct.gtf.gz (novel, 25,697); enumerate every genomic position where exactly one substitution creates an ATG; classify the created ATG's phase against the reference CDS; then compare gnomAD v4.1 observed-SNV rate and mean AF, phyloP100way mean, and ClinVar P/LP counts across phase classes. (6) Linkage: does the per-isoform model phase-contrast rank correlate with the per-gene gnomAD phase-specific depletion, at matched gene LOEUF, 5'UTR length decile and 5'UTR GC decile?
matched_reference: Three references, as trap 1 demands. (i) Method noise floor: the same ATG at phase 0, the mechanistically null phase, with identical composition and near-identical GC -- this is a within-operator null, not a different operator. (ii) Other positions: the existing 37-position frame-matched control bank (results_interp_all/bank_slot0_n500.npz), extended upstream to the same span, plus implants of AGT/GAT/GTA at the same p (same mononucleotide composition, no start codon). (iii) Matched population: for the gnomAD arm, positions in the SAME 5'UTRs and the SAME genes where one substitution creates a composition-matched non-AUG 3-mer, with gene LOEUF, 5'UTR length and GC matched -- so the contrast cannot be 'uAUG positions sit in constrained genes'.
would_refute: (a) Phase-0 implants give the same Delta as phase-1/2 -- the model reads 'an ATG' but not its frame, so the discovered element is just 'ATG', not 'oORF-creating ATG'. (b) The phase contrast vanishes in the GC-frozen arm -- it was composition (trap 2). (c) gnomAD shows equal depletion at phase-0 and phase-1/2 uAUG-creating positions -- the human population does not resolve the frame distinction, so the model's frame reading is not the biology. (d) The per-isoform gated fraction sits at 50% with a wide CI, i.e. the same near-symmetric distribution the Kozak -3 operator produced (+0.00007 median, 52.1% positive). False-negative confounder to check first (trap 7): 5'UTRs shorter than the implant span, and transcripts where the midpoint clip has eaten the upstream region, both of which silently reduce eligible p and would flatten the contrast without the model being silent.

title: Stop-to-nearest-downstream-junction spacing: the sequence branch's boundary should be the 42 nt receptive field, not the 50 nt biological rule, and ClinVar/gnomAD supply the true ruler
element: The spacing, in transcript nucleotides, between the last base of a stop codon and the nearest downstream exon-exon junction. A positional relation, which section 1 admits as a sequence element, and the single most consequential one in NMD.
test: Stage 1 (the cheap gate, one day, no downloads). Natural arm, on-manifold, no implants. Take the 7,912 reference-CDS slots with a downstream junction, restrict to those with EXACTLY ONE downstream junction so that n_downstream_ejc is constant across all distance bins by construction, and bin by stop-to-junction distance in 4 nt bins over 0-200 nt. Read the per-slot verdict g(e_r) using the classifier-inside-the-mixture decomposition the brief already validated (0.0008 AUC cost, no retraining, makes selection-vs-verdict exact) -- so no slot ablation anywhere, avoiding the attention-dilution failure that killed inference-time flag ablation. Fit the bin curve and locate the knee by segmented regression with a gene-clustered bootstrap. Window control: repeat at stop windows 500, 1000 and 2000. A receptive-field knee does not move with window width; a truncation artifact does. If there is no knee, stop -- that is already a publishable negative about the sequence branch. Stage 2 (only if a knee exists). Variant arm. From the ClinVar GRCh38 VCF take single-nucleotide nonsense variants (P/LP and B/LB separately) falling in the 16,068 ENST isoforms of the model universe; map genome -> transcript coordinate through the GENCODE GTF; implant the base; recompute the ORF's stop; rebuild the stop window from the TRUE junction table with encode_window_v5; score under (a) tabular held at the reference slot's values (sequence-only) and (b) tabular fully recomputed. Bin identically. Stage 3. Compute the empirical human curve on the same distance axis, independent of the model: fraction P/LP among ClinVar nonsense vs distance, and gnomAD v4.1 pLoF observed-count and mean AF vs distance restricted to LOEUF < 0.35 genes. The test is whether the model's sequence-only knee lands at 42 or at ~50, and whether the full-model knee lands at ~50 (it should, because n_downstream_ejc carries the rule exactly).
matched_reference: (i) Noise floor: the same binned curve computed for junctions UPSTREAM of the stop at matched absolute distance, where no EJC rule applies -- any knee there is method noise. (ii) Other positions: the same curve for stops whose nearest downstream junction lies in the last exon region, i.e. the known NMD-escaping stratum, which must be flat. (iii) Matched population: ClinVar B/LB nonsense and gnomAD common pLoF give the identical distance axis with the pathogenicity axis removed; gnomAD in particular is unannotated observational data, so it cannot inherit ClinVar's curation of the 50 nt rule.
would_refute: (a) The sequence-only curve is flat at every window width -- nothing about spacing is sequence-borne and the whole positional relation lives in n_downstream_ejc. This is a clean, architecture-predicted negative and would be worth stating outright. (b) The knee sits at 150+ nt -- then it is not the receptive field and the mechanistic story is wrong. (c) ClinVar's own empirical curve knees at 42 nt too -- then the boundary is curation, not biology; excluded by the gnomAD arm. (d) The knee moves with stop-window width -- it was truncation. Circularity guard (trap 6): this conditions on the annotated ORF, which the brief flags as circular when ORF identification is half the task. The escape is that the slot is held fixed throughout and only the stop POSITION moves within it; nothing about which ORF is selected enters either arm.

title: Conserved uORFs: does the model's uORF response track vertebrate conservation, or only the AUG-plus-stop arithmetic any 5'UTR generates?
element: The start codon and Kozak context of an upstream ORF whose span carries the conserved-uORF signature -- elevated phyloP100way over the uORF body together with in-frame preservation of its stop codon -- as against a length-, Kozak- and position-matched non-conserved uORF drawn from the same universe.
test: (1) Universe: the 16,475 isoforms with >=1 out-of-frame uORF, restricted to the ~5,913 upstream-PTC isoforms where a uORF actually occupies a slot (section 4). (2) Conservation score, computed here rather than taken from a published list: lift each uORF's transcript span to genome through the GENCODE v49 GTF (ENST) or nmd_isocall_4ct.gtf.gz (novel); take mean phyloP100way over the span; separately score the frame-preservation signature as phyloP at the uORF stop codon minus phyloP at its immediate flanking codons. Split at top vs bottom tercile on both, requiring agreement. (3) Matching, pre-registered and exact where possible: uORF length +/-10%, kozak_score level exact (it is a 3-level integer, so exact matching is cheap), uORF-stop-to-main-AUG distance +/-20%, the uORF slot's n_downstream_ejc exact, slot 0's n_downstream_ejc exact, gene LOEUF decile, 5'UTR GC decile. Matched pairs only, no regression adjustment. (4) Readout by decomposition, never by ablation: per-slot verdict g(e_r) and attention alpha_r, using the classifier-inside-the-mixture rearrangement. Slot masking is deliberately avoided -- the brief measured that inference-time ablation shrinks controls 0.66x alongside targets 0.42x, i.e. it measures attention dilution, and a matched-pair design would inherit that bias in both arms without cancelling the level. (5) Within-gene arm: for genes contributing >=2 model isoforms that share the same uORF, run the pair contrast within gene, which is the brief's own validity framework (0.919 sibling concordance; 0.803 at matched slot-0 EJC count).
matched_reference: (i) Noise floor: the identical paired contrast between two NON-conserved uORFs drawn under the same matching criteria -- a pure null that inherits every matching artifact. (ii) Other positions: the same conservation-tercile split applied to a random non-uORF 5'UTR span of equal length in the same isoforms, which must show no verdict difference; if it does, phyloP is tracking something 5'UTR-wide rather than the uORF. (iii) Matched population: LOEUF-decile matching at the gene level, so the result cannot be 'conserved uORFs sit in constrained genes with different expression and therefore different mashr labels'.
would_refute: (a) Conserved and non-conserved uORF slots have identical verdicts and identical attention at matched arithmetic -- the model's uORF response is arithmetic only. Given the 33 nt ORF floor (which excludes canonical 3-codon regulatory uORFs like ATF4 uORF1 outright) and the Kozak-tie slot selection (mean 6.3 tied at each isoform's maximum, broken by transcript order), this is a live and even likely outcome, and stating it would materially change what the paper can claim. (b) The non-uORF control span shows the same conservation split -- phyloP is a gene-level proxy, not a uORF signal. (c) The effect survives only in the unmatched comparison -- matching was doing the work. False-negative confounder to check first (trap 7): novel isoforms whose 5'UTR coordinates come from the isocall GTF rather than GENCODE may have systematically noisier genomic lift, which would blur phyloP and flatten a real contrast; run the ENST-only subset as a sensitivity arm.

title: The stop tetranucleotide as a termination-efficiency element: GC-exact TGA-vs-TAG and +4 operators, refereed by conserved-readthrough genes and by transfer to mouse orthologs
element: The four nucleotides spanning a stop codon and its immediately following base -- stop+1..stop+4 -- at a PTC. The operators are GC-exact by construction: TGA <-> TAG is a pure permutation of {T,G,A} with the G held at the same offset within the codon, and at +4 the pairs are C <-> G and A <-> T.
test: (1) ISM restricted to the three stop-codon indices and the +4 index of slot 0's stop window (the stop's middle base sits at W//2 and the codon at {W//2-1, W//2, W//2+1}, verified in data_prep.encode_transcript_orfs; +4 follows the pos_to_index convention already used in analysis_plans/measure_position_bank.py). GC-exact operators only: TGA<->TAG (the G stays at codon offset 2, so the rolling-GC channel is EXACTLY unchanged -- the only 3-mer operator in this project with a literally zero composition residual), plus +4 C<->G and A<->T, which is the operator class section 5 already validated for Kozak -3. Recompute channel 5 via recompute_gc, and run a GC-frozen arm as a second reading. (2) Frame-matched exclusions (trap 3): a +4 substitution can create a new in-frame stop one codon later or destroy a downstream ATG; report the exclusion rate per operator and drop any position whose per-operator rates differ -- the brief measured 23.6% vs 8.7% created-motif exclusion at two codon offsets, so this is not optional. (3) Pre-registered stratification by the perturbed slot's own PTC status, because section 5 already found the Kozak effect's sign follows exactly that (+0.0087 EJC-triggering vs -0.0001 not); discovering the same stratification post hoc here would be worthless. (4) External arm 1, conserved readthrough: define the readthrough set locally rather than from a published list -- elevated phyloP100way with preserved codon periodicity over the first ~60 nt of the 3'UTR, computed from the phyloP track and the GTF. Prediction: at matched n_downstream_ejc and matched ref_utr3_length decile, those genes' annotated-stop slots carry a lower verdict and a larger |Delta| under TGA<->TAG. (5) External arm 2, species transfer as the artifact control: build the identical 5-slot input for mouse GENCODE vM transcripts -- the pipeline needs only a transcript FASTA, a junction table and the five tabular numbers, all derivable from a GTF plus a genome -- run the human-trained checkpoints unchanged (section 3: no parameter depends on K and the encoder is shared, so nothing needs refitting), and apply the identical tetranucleotide operator. Prediction: the sign and rank ordering of the tetranucleotide grades transfer.
matched_reference: (i) Noise floor: the existing 37-position frame-matched control bank at the same GC-exact operators, plus the same operators applied at the +7 and +10 indices -- same frame offset, no termination role. (ii) Other positions: the annotated stop of slots whose stop is NOT EJC-triggering, where termination efficiency should carry no NMD consequence; a signal of equal size there means the effect is a nucleotide preference, not a termination readout. (iii) Matched population: the conserved-readthrough gene set matched to non-readthrough genes on n_downstream_ejc, 3'UTR length decile and LOEUF decile; and mouse, which is the population match at the species scale and the only reference in this entire brief that is outside the corpus altogether.
would_refute: (a) TGA<->TAG gives the same gated Delta as frame-matched controls. (b) The sign is opposite to the known termination grading -- e.g. TGA-C raising the NMD verdict. (c) The effect is equally present in the non-PTC stratum, so it is a general nucleotide preference. (d) Nothing transfers to mouse: the sign structure inverts or collapses. (d) is the most informative negative in the whole set, because it would say the element is corpus-specific -- and given the brief's warning (trap 7) that a confident negative here has twice been a confounder, the pre-specified confounder to rule out first is the mouse junction table: if mouse windows are built with a different junction density or 3'UTR length distribution, transfer can fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the element, so the mouse cohort must be matched to the human cohort on n_downstream_ejc and 3'UTR length before the transfer is read.

title: Purifying selection on the verdict-setting junction: are splice sites whose loss would flip the NMD call more constrained than splice sites whose loss would not?
element: The exon-exon junction lying 50-200 nt downstream of a stop codon -- the 'verdict-setting junction' -- localized to its donor and acceptor splice sites, i.e. the ~17 nt spanning the -3..+6 donor and the -12..+2 acceptor. In this dataset 1,289 reference-CDS slots have their nearest downstream junction at 50-80 nt and 2,104 at 80-150 nt, so the stratum is large.
test: (1) Use the model as a scoring function only. For each junction j in each reference-anchored isoform, compute the counterfactual verdict change from removing j: clear the channel-4 mark for j in the stop window AND decrement n_downstream_ejc -- the internally consistent joint edit. Define flip score = |Delta g(e_r)| under the per-slot-verdict decomposition. (2) Take the top and bottom deciles of flip score. (3) Match, pre-registered: MaxEnt donor and acceptor score decile (computed from sequence, so it is independent of the model), exon rank from the 3' end, exon length decile, intron length decile, gene LOEUF decile, and isoform expression decile. Matched pairs only. (4) External arm, three independent measures on the SAME +/-8 nt splice regions: gnomAD v4.1 observed-SNV density and mean AF; mean phyloP100way; ClinVar P/LP splice-region SNV counts. (5) Built-in positive control: a correct method must recover the known ~50 nt boundary as a byproduct -- junctions inside the last exon and junctions within 50 nt of the stop should fall in the low-flip decile without being told to, since that is what the ACMG PVS1 flowchart already encodes.
matched_reference: (i) Noise floor: the identical matched-pair contrast between two LOW-flip junctions, which inherits every matching artifact and must show no difference. (ii) Other positions: the same gnomAD/phyloP contrast computed over deep-intronic windows 200 nt from each junction of the same pairs, which must be null -- if it is not, the constraint is regional rather than splice-site-specific. (iii) Matched population: MaxEnt-decile matching is the load-bearing one, because strong splice sites are both more conserved and more likely to be scored as verdict-setting; without it the whole result is 'the model likes strong junctions'.
would_refute: (a) No difference in gnomAD depletion or phyloP between high-flip and low-flip junctions at matched splice strength -- the NMD consequence of a junction carries no detectable selective signature at this sample size, and the model's positional relation is invisible to selection. (b) The difference disappears once MaxEnt decile is matched -- the flip score was reading splice-site strength. (c) The deep-intronic control shows the same contrast -- it is regional constraint. (d) The method fails its own positive control by placing last-exon junctions in the high-flip decile -- then the flip score is not measuring what it claims. Ablation-adjacency, stated explicitly: this is the closest proposal here to section 6's dead 'inference-time flag ablation'. It escapes because (i) the dead method ablated is_ref_cds/is_sqanti_cds to ATTRIBUTE contribution between modalities and failed because ablation shrinks control positions 0.66x alongside targets 0.42x, i.e. it measured attention dilution; (ii) here the edit is a coherent single-junction counterfactual with the tabular count updated to match, (iii) the output is used only as a RANKING to define two sets, and (iv) all evidentiary weight is carried by gnomAD/phyloP/ClinVar, not by the magnitude of the model's Delta -- so any residual dilution bias is common to both arms of a matched pair and cannot generate the external contrast.

title: Stop-codon identity as a termination-efficiency signal, measured by the one composition-exact operator this project has
element: The identity of the terminating codon of the supplied parse — specifically the adjacent A<->G transposition at stop-codon positions 2 and 3 that carries UAG <-> UGA (window indices W/2 and W/2+1 of the stop branch).
test: Refactor analysis_plans/measure_position_bank.py to anchor on stop_windows instead of atg_windows (frame_span/eligibility must be re-derived because the stop branch clips with limit_lo=mid, not limit_hi). Sweep all four bases at W/2 and W/2+1 and cache raw per-(member, isoform, position, base) log-odds, exactly as the existing bank does, so the operator is chosen after the forward passes. Primary operator = the adjacent A<->G transposition (UAG->UGA). This is not merely GC-matched, it is multiset-identical: only ~2 entries of the 51-nt rolling-GC array change, by 1/51, versus 51 entries for UAA<->UAG, a ~25x reduction in the composition term that trap #2 says dominates every single-base operator here. Control bank: the identical adjacent A<->G transposition applied at in-frame codons elsewhere in the stop window whose positions 2-3 are {A,G} and whose first base is not T (so no stop is created or destroyed), frame-offset-matched on both arms per trap #3, spread over +/-60 and again over the downstream extent to +250. Created-AUG / created-stop exclusions enumerated per isoform before any contrast, using the existing excl logic. Conditioning arms: (i) slot-0 stop EJC-triggering vs not, at matched slot-0 attention (the same conditional that reversed the Kozak -3 sign); (ii) within mechanism class PTC+ only (n=6,864 from results_interp_all/mechanism_classes.tsv), where every stop is premature so the provenance marker is saturated and a residual effect is about termination at a PTC.
matched_reference: Comparison: the same adjacent A<->G transposition at frame-matched in-frame non-stop codons elsewhere in the same stop window of the same isoform. Matched on operator, base multiset, GC neutrality, edit distance (2 bases), codon frame offset, exclusion regime and recomputation path — everything but position. Literature anchor for the termination-efficiency hierarchy and the causal direction: Cridge, Crowe-McAuliffe, Mathew & Tate, NAR 2018 (3' nucleotides in the ribosomal mRNA channel set termination efficiency; UAA most efficient, UGA leakiest), already the reference cited at orf_model_report_v5.Rmd:1209; and Amrani et al., Nature 2004, that inefficient/aberrant termination is what triggers NMD.
would_refute: Target |t| inside the bulk of the transposition-control distribution, or members disagreeing in sign, refutes any stop-identity claim. A UNIFORM positive UGA effect with no dependence on EJC-triggering status and none surviving within PTC+ refutes the termination-efficiency reading and demotes the finding to a provenance marker — which would be a positive result for the ledger, since it retires claim 5.3.3's mechanistic gloss. A negative UGA effect present only where the slot's stop is EJC-triggering supports readthrough biology and requires the report's current interpretation to be reversed.

title: The stop tetranucleotide: +4 identity conditioned on stop identity, tested as an interaction rather than a main effect
element: The nucleotide at +4 (first base 3' of the stop, stop-window index W/2+2) in combination with the stop codon itself — the UGA-C / UAA-G tetranucleotide termination signal, plus the tandem-stop arm at +4..+6.
test: Enumerate the anchor design fully: 3 stop identities x 4 bases at +4 = 12 cells, paired within isoform, one batched forward pass per isoform per member, channel 5 recomputed on every arm and the baseline built through the same recomputation path (the measured stored-vs-recomputed offset is systematic and does not average out). Operators are re-cuts of the cached four values: G_vs_C and A_vs_T at +4, both GC-matched. The primary statistic is the difference-of-differences [ (+4 G-vs-C | UGA) - (+4 G-vs-C | UAA) ]. Exclusions: cells where the +4 substitution creates an in-frame stop at +4..+6 are removed from the primary contrast and reported as the separate tandem-stop arm (ANALYSIS4 measured 18.9% created-stop at the start anchor's +4; the stop-anchor rate must be re-measured, not assumed). Control reference: the identical 3x4 design and the identical difference-of-differences computed at every frame-matched control position in the stop-window bank of H1.
matched_reference: Comparison: the same difference-of-differences at frame-matched control positions, which should be null by construction — this cancels the documented model-wide preference for G (a main effect) that killed the start-window +4 claim, because a uniform base preference contributes identically to both halves of the interaction. Literature anchors: Namy, Hatin & Rousset, EMBO Rep 2001 (the six nucleotides 3' of the stop set termination efficiency); Loughran et al., NAR 2014 (efficient natural readthrough in mammalian genes, UGA-C contexts); Cridge et al., NAR 2018.
would_refute: The interaction lands inside the control-position interaction distribution, or the +4 G-vs-C effect is the same size at UAA and UGA anchors. Either refutes 'the model reads a tetranucleotide termination signal' and leaves only a base preference — the same verdict already reached for start-window +4, reached this time against a reference that could have shown otherwise.

title: Where is 'the' stop? A max-pool saturation test that decides whether any stop-identity result is statable as termination biology
element: The multiset of in-frame stop codons present in the stop window's downstream extent, versus the single terminating codon at the anchor.
test: Three arms on the H1 cache plus one extra sweep. (a) Stratify the per-isoform H1 effect by presence/absence of a downstream in-frame stop of the substituted identity within the window, matched on n_downstream_ejc, mechanism class and window GC decile. (b) Transplant profile: apply the same adjacent A<->G transposition to in-frame UAG codons at distances d in {+21, +42, +84, +150, +250, +400} downstream of the anchor, one d per pass, and plot per-isoform |Delta| against d with the anchor as d=0 of the same profile. (c) Frame control at every d: the identical transposition applied to the same bases shifted by 1 nt, so the triplet is out of frame — identical base multiset, identical local arrangement up to a 1-nt shift, the only systematic difference being whether channels 6-8 mark the triplet as in-frame.
matched_reference: Comparison: (i) the anchor is d=0 of the same distance profile under the identical operator, so target and reference differ only in position; (ii) the 1-nt-shifted out-of-frame arm at each d holds base content constant and varies only frame-channel register. Architectural reference: the brief's own verified facts — global max over the length axis, conv2 receptive field 42 nt, mid-pool quantisation to 4 nt.
would_refute: An anchor effect undiminished by a pre-existing downstream in-frame stop TOGETHER WITH a near-zero downstream transplant effect refutes the delocalization hypothesis. That outcome is the more interesting one: it would mean the model does localize the terminating codon despite global max pooling, which licenses reading H1 and H2 as biology about termination rather than about 3' composition. Confirming delocalization means H1/H2 must be restated as 'in-frame stop-codon content of the 3' region', which is a weaker but still nameable sequence property.

title: Readthrough escape geometry: the next in-frame stop, and whether a junction sits between it and the supplied stop
element: The position and identity of the FIRST in-frame stop codon downstream of the supplied stop, and the count of exon junctions in the interval between the two.
test: Operator is a mononucleotide-preserving permutation, which is explicitly NOT the dead dinucleotide-preserving 3-mer shuffle (that was the identity map because all 64 3-mers have exactly one dinucleotide-preserving arrangement; a mononucleotide-preserving permutation of UAG has 5 alternatives, of which AGU/GUA/GAU are valid after excluding UGA as still-a-stop and AUG as a created start). Permute the first downstream in-frame stop to a valid non-stop arrangement of the same three bases, exclusions enumerated per isoform for created AUGs and created stops in any frame within the local 5-mer. Then stratify by whether the NEXT in-frame stop after the destroyed one lies beyond vs before the last junction in the window, and form the difference of differences. Controls: (i) the identical permutation applied at the 1-nt-shifted out-of-frame position — identical base multiset, no stop destroyed; (ii) the identical permutation applied in isoforms where the interval to the last junction does not change classification.
matched_reference: Comparison: the same permutation at a 1-nt-shifted out-of-frame position in the same isoform (composition-identical, frame-register-different), and the same permutation in isoforms whose junction classification is unchanged by it. Literature anchors: Loughran et al., NAR 2014 and Schueren & Thoms, PLoS Genet 2016 for readthrough producing C-terminally extended products terminating at the next in-frame stop; Karousis & Muhlemann, CSH Perspect Biol 2019 (already cited in this repo) for NMD beginning where translation ends.
would_refute: No difference between the two junction-geometry strata — the model treats destruction of a downstream in-frame stop identically regardless of whether the readthrough termination site would cross the last junction. Given global max pooling and the 42-nt conv2 receptive field, this negative is the likely outcome, and it is informative rather than empty: it localizes a real, nameable relation that the current architecture cannot represent, and makes a concrete retraining recommendation (a downstream-in-frame-stop channel, or a receptive field wide enough to span the interval) rather than a null claim about biology.

title: Poly(A)-signal proximity to the supplied stop, tested by composition-exact hexamer permutation
element: The AAUAAA hexamer downstream of the supplied stop and its distance from it — the faux-3'UTR / PABPC1-proximity element.
test: Seven arms at each of d in {+10, +30, +60, +120, +250, +500}: implant AAUAAA, and separately implant each of the five other distinct arrangements of the multiset A5U1 (AAAAAU, AAAAUA, AAAUAA, AAUAAA excluded as target, AUAAAA, UAAAAA). All arms have identical mononucleotide composition and zero GC, so channel 5 is identical across arms up to boundary effects at the two edges of the 51-nt rolling support — the composition confound that trap #2 says dominates is removed by construction, not adjusted for. Run at atg2000_stop2000 so the stop window reaches +1001 and the larger d values are unpadded (ANALYSIS4 measured the stop branch reportable to +501 at W=1000 and +1001 at W=2000). Additional arms: (i) the identical implant at matched distance UPSTREAM of the stop, inside the ORF, where a PAS has no termination meaning but the composition change is identical; (ii) a saturation arm restricted to isoforms that already carry an AAUAAA/AUUAAA within the window, as in H3.
matched_reference: Comparison: the five composition-identical permuted hexamers at the identical position in the identical isoform. Matched on mononucleotide composition exactly, on GC exactly, on position exactly, on isoform exactly — arrangement is the only thing that varies. Secondary reference: the same implant upstream of the stop inside the ORF, where the motif is not a termination signal. Literature anchors: Amrani et al., Nature 2004 (faux 3'UTR promotes aberrant termination and triggers NMD); Silva, Ribeiro, Inacio, Liebhaber & Romao, RNA 2008 (PABPC1 proximity to a PTC inhibits mammalian NMD).
would_refute: AAUAAA indistinguishable from its own permutations at every d. That is the likely outcome if the model reads only composition, and it would be a clean, defensible negative on the only order-specific (non-compositional) motif claim in this project: with composition exactly matched, a null cannot be blamed on the GC channel. A positive would be the first arrangement-specific motif finding here and carries a distance profile with it.

title: The stop-to-junction distance relation is computed from sequence, and its ruler is the receptive field
element: An exon-exon junction mark (channel 4) lying d nt downstream of the ORF's stop codon; the relation "nearest downstream junction within d of the stop", with d swept 1-400 nt.
test: Junction-sliding assay on the stop window. Restrict to slots with exactly one channel-4 mark inside the stop window and >=200 nt of filled window on each side of the stop. Relocate that single mark to each d on a grid (1 nt steps over 1-80, 4 nt steps over 80-400), leaving channels 0-3, 5 and 6-8 untouched and holding the entire tabular block fixed at its observed value in every condition. Mirror arm: relocate the same mark to -d, upstream of the stop, inside the filled upstream extent. Readout is the slot's own conditional verdict v_r = cls_head(ReLU(head[0](e_r))), which is exactly what a one-hot attention vector on slot r returns from the unmodified model, so attention dilution cannot enter (this is why the section-6 flag-ablation failure mode does not apply). Five members, n ~2,000 isoforms. Positive control run in the same harness: shift the normalised n_downstream_ejc by 1 SD and confirm it moves v_r by orders of magnitude above the floor, so a flat sliding profile is a real null and not a dead readout.
matched_reference: Three, as trap 1 requires. (a) The upstream mirror at matched |d| - same window, same branch weights, same slot, same isoform, same single mark, same fixed tabular block; only downstream junctions are supposed to count, so the asymmetry IS the claim. (b) The method's own floor: relocating the mark back to its observed index is a no-op, and the same harness measured no-op |effect| max 1.4e-6 at n=500. (c) The architectural ceiling as an independent reference: no stop-junction co-detection is representable past 42 nt, so a smooth ramp extending to 100+ nt cannot be the proposed mechanism and indicts the measurement rather than confirming the biology.
would_refute: v_r(d) flat across the whole downstream arm within the 1.4e-6 floor, and indistinguishable from the upstream mirror, while the n_downstream_ejc positive control moves v_r by >>floor. That is a clean negative with a real consequence: the ~43% of the decision carried by the EJC count (structural 59-78% x EJC 61-64% within it) would be a number handed to the model that it never reconstructs from sequence, and the paper's "learns NMD rules from sequence" framing would need revision. A knee well beyond 45 nt would also refute the stated mechanism, since the architecture cannot represent it.

title: Kozak -3 is an initiation-efficiency signal: it acts on the verdict only through ORF selection
element: The -3 purine of a candidate AUG, measured under the GC-matched A-vs-T operator (and cross-checked under G-vs-C), at index W/2-4 of the start window.
test: Exact two-way counterfactual decomposition on the TRUE model, not the factorized approximation. From one baseline pass keep the per-slot embeddings e0 and attentions alpha0; from the perturbed pass keep e1, alpha1. Then evaluate the head on three recombinations: g(sum alpha1*e0) = selection-only, g(sum alpha0*e1) = verdict-only, g(sum alpha1*e1) = both. The residual is the MEASURED interaction, not an assumed additivity - and this is exactly the failure that killed DeepSHAP here (completeness error 129-307%), avoided because these are forward evaluations, not attributions. Recombination is a 64-dim matmul, so the marginal cost over the existing bank sweep is ~zero; the encoder passes are the ones already being run. Report the factorized reading sum_r alpha_r*v_r (probe_head_swap.py, dAUC -0.0008, rank corr 0.9995) as the interpretable cross-check, with its exactness condition (mixed-sign hidden units) reported per isoform since it is already computed there.
matched_reference: The 37 frame-matched control positions carry the identical decomposition under the identical GC-matched operator, giving both the "other positions" reference and, through the interaction term's spread, the method's noise floor. Operator cross-check: a real base-identity effect must appear in both A_vs_T and G_vs_C (each individually GC-neutral) and must NOT be reproduced by GC_vs_AT, which isolates the composition confound. Population reference: strata by the perturbed slot's own PTC status and by attention tercile, both already implemented in analyse_position_bank.py, because the mechanism predicts the sign flip in each.
would_refute: The verdict term at -3 is comparable to or larger than the selection term, or the per-isoform sign prediction P2 does no better at -3 than at the control positions. Either kills the initiation-efficiency reading: -3 would be changing what the parse means rather than whether it is used, and the interpretation of attention as an ORF-selection probability would lose its main empirical support. A large measured interaction term would also refute the decomposition itself and would have to be reported as such.

title: Termination efficiency at the stop: readthrough context modulates decay only where the stop is EJC-triggering
element: The stop tetranucleotide - specifically the base immediately 3' of the stop codon (stop-window index W/2+2) under the GC-matched C-vs-G operator, and secondarily the stop codon's own third base (TAA vs TAG).
test: Single-base substitution at W/2+2 under C-vs-G (the only operator class measured here to have a near-null control reference, trap 2), carrying the position bank's existing created-motif exclusions - a substitution creating a new in-frame stop or a new AUG within +/-2 is dropped, and complete-case only, since a partially excluded side becomes a different operator. Readout is the slot's own conditional verdict v_r, not the transcript logit, which removes attention dilution - the exact confounder that made the flag-ablation result uninterpretable. Primary statistic is a difference-in-differences across the perturbed slot's own PTC status, using build_mechanism_classes.py's window-width-independent PTC call (junction >50 nt past the stop, reference-AUG anchored). Because the C-vs-G GC change is identical in both arms of the DiD, the composition term cancels by construction. Secondary: TAA->TAG (A->G at W/2+1) with the same DiD, where composition cancellation is the only defence available since no stop-identity contrast is GC-neutral.
matched_reference: (a) Frame-matched control positions in the same 3'UTR arm of the same stop window under the identical C-vs-G operator; the created-motif exclusion rate depends on codon offset (23.6% vs 8.7% measured), so controls must share +4's offset. (b) The PTC- slot population as the matched population for the interaction, matched additionally on 3'UTR length, window-local GC and observed base, since PTC+ and PTC- slots differ systematically in all three. (c) The 1.4e-6 no-op floor from the same harness.
would_refute: Delta_v_r at +4 sits inside the control-position distribution, or the PTC+ / PTC- difference-in-differences is null while the positive control (a PTC-status manipulation of the junction geometry) moves v_r strongly. Also refuting: an effect of equal size at all three stop codons and at both PTC statuses, which would mean the model is reading local composition at the window centre rather than termination context.

title: An out-of-frame AUG inside the ORF body is the within-slot signature of an overlapping ORF
element: An AUG trinucleotide located between a candidate upstream ORF's start and that ORF's midpoint, in a reading frame other than the candidate's own - i.e. an A,T,G in channels 0-3 coinciding with a non-zero frame channel (7 or 8) in the start window.
test: Two stages, the first a screen and the second the causal test. (i) Screen: compare v_r (per-slot conditional verdict) for upstream-ORF slots in the oORF class against the 5'UTR-terminating class from build_mechanism_classes.py, matched on n_downstream_ejc, ORF length and frac_start. If the classes are indistinguishable, stop - there is nothing to localise. (ii) Intervention: GC-matched destruction of the specific internal out-of-frame AUG that coincides with the reference-projected CDS start, by A->T at codon position 1 or G->C at position 3 (both GC-neutral, so channel 5 is invariant and trap 2 does not bite), with the standard created-motif exclusions. Measure Delta_v_r for the upstream-ORF slot only; the same base in other slots' windows is a separate array copy and is deliberately left untouched, which is what attributes the effect to this parse. Report the propagated (all-slots) substitution as a sensitivity, since window-local editing is the off-manifold version.
matched_reference: (a) Destruction of OTHER out-of-frame AUGs in the same window, at matched distance from the candidate start and matched codon offset - same operator, same exclusions, same GC neutrality, differing only in whether the AUG is the annotated main start. (b) Destruction of IN-FRAME internal AUGs, which by the biology are N-terminal extension starts and not competing ORFs at all. (c) The frame-matched control positions already in the bank, as the noise floor. The (a) contrast is the load-bearing one: it is matched on everything except the element's identity.
would_refute: Stage (i) null: oORF and 5'UTR-uORF slots have indistinguishable v_r at matched geometry. Or stage (ii) null: destroying the main-start out-of-frame AUG moves v_r no more than destroying a decoy out-of-frame AUG.
